title: "A" nurse
description: Stroke, fractures and bleeding, dressings, Lifepak, blood glucose, basic CPR. No medicines, no IV.

questions.q: What does the FAST acronym mean in stroke recognition?
answers: Face, Arm, Speech, Time
Face, Arm, Sight, Temperature
Facial droop, Ataxia, Sensation, Tone
Focus, Awareness, Speech, Tremor

questions.q: Which finding of the neuro exam points to a stroke?
answers: Drooping on one side of the face and slurred speech
Pinpoint pupils on both sides and very slow breathing
Bitten tongue, wet trousers and confusion that slowly clears
Sweating, shaking and confusion that develop within minutes

questions.q: What must you always measure when you suspect a stroke, because it can cause similar signs?
answers: Blood glucose
Body temperature
Oxygen saturation
Blood pressure on both arms

questions.q: Why is a stroke time-critical?
answers: Untreated it gets worse every few minutes and only a hospital can treat it
The swelling of the brain stops breathing within minutes in almost every case
The blood pressure falls quickly, so the patient goes into shock on scene
It is not, but the patient must be seen by a doctor on the same day

questions.q: Which systolic blood pressure is accepted on scene when a stroke is suspected?
answers: 130–220 mmHg, we do not force it down
100–140 mmHg, higher values are lowered
90–120 mmHg, to protect against bleeding
Anything above 160 mmHg must be lowered

questions.q: Severe bleeding from a limb. What is the first step?
answers: Direct pressure on the wound, then a pressure bandage
Raise the limb above the heart, then a loose dressing
Splint the limb so that the bleeding vessel stays still
Cool the wound with cold water to narrow the vessels

questions.q: A gunshot wound is bleeding heavily. What is the basis of the care?
answers: Stopping the bleeding with a pressure bandage
Searching for and removing the bullet on scene
Splinting the limb before anything else is done
Cleaning the wound well, then a loose dressing

questions.q: The bandage bleeds through. What do you do?
answers: Add another layer and press harder, do not remove the first one
Remove the soaked bandage and put a fresh, tighter one on the wound
Loosen the bandage a little, because it is too tight and bleeds more
Remove it, clean the wound to find the source, then bandage again

questions.q: Which is the sign of an open fracture?
answers: The bone breaks through the skin and the wound bleeds
Heavy swelling and a large bruise over the broken bone
The limb is clearly deformed or shorter than the other
Grating of the bone ends is felt when the limb is moved

questions.q: How do you immobilise a forearm fracture?
answers: The splint fixes the joint above and below the fracture
The splint covers only the fracture so the joints can move
Straighten the arm fully first, then splint it in that way
Fix only the wrist, the elbow must stay free to move it

questions.q: What do you check before and after splinting?
answers: Circulation, feeling and movement of the limb below the fracture
Swelling, bruising and pain of the limb right over the fracture
Pulse, blood pressure and SpO2 of the patient on the monitor
Circulation, feeling and movement of the limb above the fracture

questions.q: How do you treat a burned skin area?
answers: With a sterile, non-stick dressing
With a tight pressure bandage over it
By opening the blisters, then a dressing
With burn ointment, then a cotton pad

questions.q: A burned patient is hoarse, has soot around the mouth and a falling SpO2. What do you think of?
answers: An airway burn: advanced (ALS) care is needed
Smoke irritation: oxygen and a dressing are enough
Panic and pain: calm the patient and dress the burns
A large skin burn: the pain makes the breathing worse

questions.q: Where do the defibrillator (Lifepak) pads go?
answers: One under the right collarbone, one on the left side of the lower chest
One under the left collarbone, one on the right side of the lower chest
One on the middle of the breastbone, one on the right side of the chest
Both on the left side of the chest, one above and one below the nipple

questions.q: After attaching the monitor, what do you see besides the pulse?
answers: The rhythm, the SpO2 and the blood pressure
The rhythm, the SpO2 and the blood glucose
The SpO2, the temperature and the pupil reaction
The rhythm, the blood glucose and the temperature

questions.q: What is the rule during the AED rhythm analysis and the shock?
answers: Nobody touches the patient
Compressions continue, only the breaths stop
One person holds the pads firmly on the chest
Only the ventilation continues with the bag

questions.q: What is the compression to ventilation ratio in adult CPR?
At what rate do you do chest compressions?
answers: 100–120 per minute
80–100 per minute
120–140 per minute
60–80 per minute

questions.q: What is the normal blood glucose at rest?
answers: About 70–100 mg/dL (3.9–5.6 mmol/L)
About 40–60 mg/dL (2.2–3.3 mmol/L)
About 120–160 mg/dL (6.7–8.9 mmol/L)
About 180–220 mg/dL (10–12.2 mmol/L)

questions.q: From what value is the blood glucose low?
answers: Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L)
Below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L)
Below 40 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L)
Below 120 mg/dL (6.7 mmol/L)

questions.q: The glucometer shows this. What does it mean?
answers: Severe hypoglycaemia, sugar is needed at once
Slightly low, check it again in 30 minutes
A normal fasting value, no action is needed
High blood glucose, the patient needs insulin

questions.q: What are the signs of low blood glucose?
answers: Sweating, shaking, pale skin, confusion, fast pulse
Dry warm skin, deep fast breathing, fruity breath
Great thirst, frequent urination, dry mouth, fatigue
Slow pulse, pinpoint pupils, slow shallow breathing

questions.q: When do you put on an oxygen mask?
answers: When the SpO2 is low or the patient is short of breath
For every patient with chest pain, even with good SpO2
Only when the SpO2 falls below 80% and nothing else
Only for an unconscious patient who breathes normally

questions.q: What is the target oxygen saturation for most acute patients?
Unconscious patient who breathes well, no suspected spine injury. How do you position them?
answers: Recovery position
On the back, legs raised
Half sitting, back supported
On the back, head turned aside

questions.q: How deep do you press the chest in adult CPR?
answers: 5–6 cm
3–4 cm
7–8 cm
4–5 cm
